title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Solaris Health through Redwood Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdowns. Discussed token-level cost, routing policies, caching, batch settings, and how to attribute costs to product routes. Customer asked about SOC2, SSO/SAML, VPC/private deployment and dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Agreed next steps: send pricing sheet, security docs, and schedule a 1-week pilot to run benchmarks with their sample traffic.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 09:32 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Solaris Head of ML), Daniel Park (Solaris Infra), Sophie Lee (Procurement)

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, um, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya, our solutions engineer. Today we'll run through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and a cost breakdown, and then leave time for questions.
[00:00:12] Maya: Thanks Alex, we got about 45 minutes, we want to see how we'd map our product routes and understand the cost implications before we go to procurement.
[00:00:20] Priya: Great, I'll share my screen — tell me if you can see the Console.
[00:00:30] Sophie: I can see it, looks good.
[00:00:35] Priya: Cool. So first page is the Usage Overview — token volume over time, latency distribution, error rates. You'll notice top-right there's a filter for model and route. We typically map routes to product features, like 'search-autocomplete' or 'support-chat'.
[00:00:55] Daniel: Quick Q — when you say token volume, is that request+response tokens or just input?
[00:01:02] Priya: It's both, we show input, output and total tokens. The cost engine attributes cost per token based on the model variant used — so if a request hits a smaller quantized variant that's cheaper, the per-token price applies there.
[00:01:18] Maya: That attribution, does it do per-route cost breakdowns automatically or do we need to tag requests?
[00:01:25] Priya: You can do either. By default we use the 'route' header that matches the API route name. If you want custom attribution we recommend adding a x-redwood-route or using the SDK which sets route metadata.
[00:01:40] Alex: And on the billing side we can break down by model, route, or team — depends on what you need for chargebacks.
[00:01:48] Maya: Nice. Can you show an example where a high-latency spike maps to a cost anomaly?
[00:01:55] Priya: Sure — over here is a per-route dashboard for 'triage-bot' where you can see token counts, P50/P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:02:10] [00:02:15] Priya: (narrating) You'll see at 2/25 there was a spike in output tokens because the prompt template changed; Console surfaces that as an anomaly and we link to the prompt set and recent deployments.
[00:02:30] Daniel: Hmm, prompt template changed — do you keep a history of template versions so we can roll back?
[00:02:37] Priya: Yes, Console integrates with our model rollout history and prompt set config — you can pin prompt versions per-route. There's also an eval view to run regression tests against baseline prompts.
[00:02:49] Maya: For our compliance team we need audit logs of who changed a route setting. Is that in Console?
[00:02:55] Alex: Yep, audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private customers — they include the actor, timestamp and diffs. We also support SSO/SAML and granular RBAC.
[00:03:05] Sophie: Good. Procurement will want SOC 2.
[00:03:09] Alex: We are SOC 2 Type II certified. We'll send the security package after the call.
[00:03:14] Maya: Perfect.
[00:03:20] [00:03:30] Priya: Back to cost — here's the per-route cost breakdown. On the left is runtime cost (GPU, reserved capacity amortization), middle is model cost per-token and right is total cost including caching and network. The Console can attribute costs based on sampling or exact attribution depending on your accuracy needs.
[00:03:50] Daniel: Sampling? explain that quickly — we need accurate chargebacks for our internal teams.
[00:03:57] Priya: Right, so exact attribution means every request is tagged and cost is measured per-request. Sampling uses a statistically representative subset to reduce telemetry overhead. For most customers, sampling at 5-10% yields sub-1% error on cost estimates but with much lower overhead.
[00:04:13] Maya: Ok that's helpful. Does Redwood show suggestions on optimizations?
[00:04:18] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend batching thresholds, cache TTLs, and model quantization profiles per workload. In the Console you can click 'Optimize' and get suggested config changes with estimated cost delta.
[00:04:32] [00:04:40] Priya: For example, Optimize detected that 'billing-invoice-route' could benefit from a small prompt cache for common prefixes — estimated 22% cost savings and negligible latency impact.
[00:04:55] Maya: Is that suggestion safe for healthcare data? we have PHI concerns.
[00:05:00] Alex: Good callout. For PHI, we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, and we can disable cross-request caching. All infra-level controls are configurable.
[00:05:12] Sophie: On the KMS — do you support our cloud KMS (GCP KMS)?
[00:05:16] Alex: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated.
[00:05:22] Daniel: Latency SLOs — if we commit to 95ms p95 for short responses, how does Dedicated help vs hosted?
[00:05:30] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better isolation, so variability is lower and p95 is more predictable. Hosted can hit lower median latency but with more variance depending on multi-tenant load. We also have routing policies to favor low-latency variants for critical routes.
[00:05:46] [00:06:00] Maya: Let's talk concrete numbers — can you show me cost per 1k tokens for gpt-like model vs a quantized 7B variant?
[00:06:08] Priya: On the console the model catalog includes verified performance profiles. Example: gpt-xxl-ish model = $0.18 per 1k tokens, 7B quantized variant = $0.012 per 1k tokens (example numbers; final pricing varies by contract). The dashboard can show weighted averages based on the mix of model calls per route.
[00:06:29] Maya: Great — and do you show token breakdown by prompt template so we can identify expensive prompts?
[00:06:33] Priya: Yes, Prompt Insights highlights templates with highest output tokens and link them back to routes and deployments.
[00:06:40] [00:07:00] Sophie: Procurement wants to know contract terms for Dedicated — minimum commit, ability to burst, and SLAs.
[00:07:07] Alex: Dedicated typically has monthly reserved capacity with burst buckets and SLA for uptime and latency tiers. We'll include the sample contract in the follow-up.
[00:07:15] Sophie: Perfect.
[00:07:20] Daniel: For our POC we'd like to run a benchmark with our traffic profile — can Redwood emulate our mix of short few-token queries and long-context generation?
[00:07:29] Priya: Absolutely. We can run a 1-week pilot in Dedicated or a hosted pilot with performance telemetry. We'll ingest a synthetic workload derived from your logs — privacy preserved — and run head-to-head comparisons.
[00:07:43] Maya: Is there an easy way to tag traffic to map it to product teams?
[00:07:47] Priya: There's a route header plus you can add metadata fields like team_id; Console accepts those and you can slice dashboards by metadata.
[00:07:58] [00:08:15] Priya: Now I'll demo the per-route cost drilldown — clicking a route shows timeline, token mix, model variants used, caching hits and last 50 requests sample.
[00:08:26] [00:08:30] Priya: (mumble) you'll also see the KV cache hit ratio, when the cache was seeded and if it caused a decrease in output tokens.
[00:08:40] Maya: That KV cache — is it prefix caching? how does it affect correctness?
[00:08:44] Priya: It's prefix and KV caching; we respect TTLs and keys, and you can opt to disable semantic caching if you need strict determinism.
[00:08:55] [00:09:10] Alex: Another thing — the Console has cost allocation packs for FinOps teams where you can export a daily CSV of per-route costs, model usage and raw token counts.
[00:09:20] Daniel: Export formats? we want to plug into our internal chargeback pipeline.
[00:09:24] Priya: CSV, Parquet, and we have a webhook ingest that can push daily summaries to your data lake.
[00:09:32] Maya: Good.
[00:09:40] [00:10:00] Priya: Moving on — I'll open the Optimize recommendations for this account. The UI shows potential savings, estimated impact on latency and a confidence score.
[00:10:12] Maya: Confidence score, how is that calculated?
[00:10:15] Priya: It's based on past outcomes of similar workloads and a simulation of your payload distribution. Lower confidence means we strongly recommend a pilot, not an immediate swap.
[00:10:26] [00:10:40] Daniel: For model fallbacks — if you route to a cheaper variant and latency increases occasionally, can you have an automatic fallback to the higher-perf model?
[00:10:48] Priya: Yes, routing policies support latency-first or cost-first modes, and automatic fallback if p90 breach or error rates go above threshold.
[00:10:58] Maya: We have healthcare compliance windows where we can't use multi-tenant models for certain data. Can we mix modes?
[00:11:05] Alex: You can define per-route policies: routes that accept PHI go to Dedicated/Private only, others use hosted for cost savings.
[00:11:15] [00:11:30] Sophie: Anything else procurement needs to know? data residency, right?
[00:11:35] Alex: Yes, we support region pinning and data residency options for enterprise customers.
[00:11:40] [00:12:00] Maya: Ok — show me what a PoC would look like — timeline and success criteria.
[00:12:05] Priya: Pilot scope: 1 week load test, ingest synthetic traffic, measure p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and functional correctness on a small eval set. Success criteria example: p95 < 120ms for short responses, cost per 1M tokens within X% of target, and no regression on eval prompts.
[00:12:28] Maya: Who runs the pilot? do we need an engineer on your side?
[00:12:33] Priya: We'll provide an SE contact (me) to set up and monitor. You'll provide anonymized logs and a contact who can authorize test traffic.
[00:12:44] [00:13:00] Sophie: Anything around security review? we'll loop in InfoSec.
[00:13:04] Alex: We'll share SOC 2 reports, encryption docs, and a security questionnaire. We can also do an architecture whiteboard session with your InfoSec.
[00:13:15] Sophie: Great.
[00:13:25] [00:13:45] (small crosstalk as Priya navigates)
[00:13:50] Priya: Quick note, small transcription glitch — the Console labels sometimes show 'redwood optimize' as 'redwood optimizer' in older exports.
[00:13:58] Maya: (laughs) totally fine.
[00:14:05] [00:14:30] Daniel: One technical thing — how does KV cache persist across nodes? if we have Dedicated multi-AZ, is the KV cache shared?
[00:14:38] Priya: We offer an option: ephemeral per-shard cache for ultra-low latency or a shared distributed KV for higher hit rates. For Dedicated we recommend shared KV with replication.
[00:14:52] Maya: Does replication add latencies?
[00:14:56] Priya: Minimal, and we can colocate caches to reduce cross-AZ hops.
[00:15:05] [00:15:20] Maya: Ok, timebox question — what's the expected unit cost improvement if we adopt Optimize suggestions?
[00:15:26] Priya: Typical customers see 15-40% improvements depending on workload shape. If you have a lot of repetitive prompts, caching helps a ton; if it's high-creative outputs, quantization and batching help less.
[00:15:40] Maya: That's a wide range but helpful.
[00:15:50] [00:16:00] Sophie: Procurement will want to see a sample cost model — can you share a per-route example showing pre/post savings?
[00:16:07] Alex: Yes, we'll include a sample spreadsheet that maps routes to cost lines and shows estimated savings from Optimize recommendations.
[00:16:15] Sophie: Thank you.
[00:16:22] [00:16:40] Priya: I'm going to open the Alerts tab — you can set anomaly alerts on token surges, latency breaches, and sudden model drift detected by our eval hooks.
[00:16:52] Maya: Model drift detection, can you elaborate?
[00:16:55] Priya: We run automated evals on a holdout prompt set; if the generation quality on key prompts drops beyond a threshold we alert and link to recent model rollouts or prompt changes.
[00:17:08] Maya: That would be super useful during canary rollouts.
[00:17:12] [00:17:30] Daniel: We use K8s for infra, any integration there?
[00:17:35] Alex: For Private deployments we provide Helm charts and operator integrations; for Dedicated we have a Kubernetes-based control plane in our infra, but your app can remain unchanged and call our API.
[00:17:47] Daniel: Great.
[00:17:55] [00:18:20] Alex: Let's recap next steps and responsibilities.
[00:18:26] Maya: Go ahead.
[00:18:30] Alex: We'll send: 1) pricing sheet and sample per-route cost model, 2) security docs (SOC 2, KMS integration guide), 3) sample contract for Dedicated and burst terms, 4) propose pilot dates for a 1-week benchmark.
[00:18:47] Sophie: Procurement will need the contract and an MSA.
[00:18:50] Alex: We'll attach a draft MSA.
[00:18:54] Daniel: From our side we'll prepare anonymized logs and identify an engineer to coordinate tests.
[00:18:59] Maya: I'll assemble stakeholders for the pilot and circle back with available dates.
[00:19:05] [00:19:20] Priya: Any final technical questions?
[00:19:25] Maya: Not right now, I think we covered everything — this was helpful.
[00:19:30] Sophie: Thanks Alex and Priya.
[00:19:34] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and proposed pilot next business day.
[00:19:40] (call ends)
